cues.en: Mamorpeggers.
cues.zh: MMORPG玩家。

cues.en: Also known as massively multiplayer
cues.zh: 也叫大型多人在线

cues.en: online role playing games, Mamorpeggers is a phonetic pronunciation of the acronym that I made up. This genre carries an enormous amount of potential, the bulk of which is currently being wasted, which is good for me because it gives me something to complain about.
cues.zh: 角色扮演游戏，Mamorpeggers是我编的缩写谐音读法。这个品类潜力巨大，但目前大部分都被浪费了，这对我倒是好事，因为我有东西可以吐槽了。

cues.en: How is its potential being wasted? In order to answer that question, I'm going to make use of an elaborate analogy.
cues.zh: 它的潜力是怎么被浪费的？为了回答这个问题，我要用一个精心设计的类比。

cues.en: Part one, an elaborate analogy.
cues.zh: 第一部分，一个精心设计的类比。

cues.en: Let's turn the clock back to 1984,
cues.zh: 让我们把时钟拨回1984年，

cues.en: the rookie year of an obscure, little known NBA player named Michael Jordan.
cues.zh: 那是名不见经传的NBA新秀迈克尔·乔丹的新人年。

cues.en: Stay with me here. This is the analogy I was talking about.
cues.zh: 请耐心听我说完。这就是我刚才提到的那个类比。

cues.en: Michael Jordan was a great basketball player who also ruined basketball for a generation.
cues.zh: 迈克尔·乔丹是一位伟大的篮球运动员，但他也让一代人对篮球失去了热情。

cues.en: It's not his fault. He didn't do it on purpose. He didn't mean to ruin basketball,
cues.zh: 这不是他的错。他不是故意的。他并不想毁掉篮球，

cues.en: but he did.
cues.zh: 但他确实做到了。

cues.en: Not because of what he did on the court. On the court, he did most everything right. He won six NBA titles. He led the league in scoring like fifty years in a row. He teamed up with Bugs Bunny and Dan Aykroyd to defeat the Monstars and he was voted the league's most valuable player five times.
cues.zh: 不是因为他球场上的所作所为。在球场上，他几乎做的一切都是对的。他赢得了六个NBA总冠军。他连续五十年领跑联盟得分榜。他和兔八哥、丹·艾克罗伊德联手击败了怪兽队，还五次当选联盟最有价值球员。

cues.en: But while he was doing all that, Michael Jordan the actual person dissolved into the ether and was replaced by Michael Jordan the Nike product.
cues.zh: 但在他做这一切的时候，迈克尔·乔丹这个真实的人渐渐消散，取而代之的是作为耐克产品的迈克尔·乔丹。

cues.en: And when you're Michael Jordan, the Nike product, just being good isn't good enough. You have to be a mythical figure. The mythical Jordan, the personality template against which all other athletes are judged.
cues.zh: 而当你成为耐克产品迈克尔·乔丹时，仅仅优秀还不够，你必须成为一个神话般的人物。神话中的乔丹，一个供所有其他运动员评判参照的人格模板。

cues.en: Anything less would have sold slightly fewer overpriced sneakers.
cues.zh: 稍逊一筹，就会少卖几双价格虚高的运动鞋。

cues.en: Before Jordan, there were as many great player personalities as there were great players. You had the grace and thoughtful reserve of Kareem Abdul Jabbar, the surly but somehow endearing arrogance of Larry Bird, and the infectious joy and daring of Magic Johnson.
cues.zh: 在乔丹之前，伟大球员的个性如同伟大球员一样多。有卡里姆·阿卜杜勒·贾巴尔的优雅与深思熟虑的矜持，有拉里·伯德那种暴躁却莫名讨人喜欢的傲慢，还有魔术师约翰逊那种富有感染力的快乐与大胆。

cues.en: But afterwards, there was only one acceptable personality,
cues.zh: 但在这之后，只有一种可接受的个性，

cues.en: the carefully packaged and deliberately commodified one of the mythical Jordan.
cues.zh: 那就是神话般的乔丹精心包装、刻意商品化的个性。

cues.en: Bland, uncontroversial,
cues.zh: 平淡无奇、毫无争议，

cues.en: mostly humorless, hyper competitive, hyper focused.
cues.zh: 大多缺乏幽默感、极度好胜、极度专注。

cues.en: We, and by we I mean ESPN,
cues.zh: 我们，我说的我们是指ESPN，

cues.en: even had to create an entire new language of obnoxious terms to describe this monster they'd created and our entire conception of basketball and even of team sports in general was rewritten to accommodate it.
cues.zh: 甚至不得不创造一整套令人反感的新术语，来描述他们创造出的这个怪物，而我们整个篮球观、乃至对团队运动的整体认知，都被改写来适应它。

cues.en: Individual scoring was overvalued,
cues.zh: 个人得分被高估了，

cues.en: efficient use of possessions was undervalued and ball hogging in the fourth quarter went from vice to virtue.
cues.zh: 回合的高效利用被低估了，第四节独霸球权从恶习变成了美德。

cues.en: The mythical Jordan became the athletic equivalent of a Jungian archetype,
cues.zh: 神话般的Jordan成了运动界的荣格原型，

cues.en: a template we impose on ourselves and others without even realizing it. Whenever a star player loses the big game, we look for the ways in which he isn't Jordan enough. And whenever a star player who's never won the big game before finally wins it, we look for the ways in which he became more Jordan than he was before.
cues.zh: 一个我们不自觉套在自己和他人身上的模板。每当明星球员输掉关键比赛，我们就找他哪里不够Jordan。每当从未赢过关键比赛的明星球员终于夺冠，我们就找他哪里比以前更像Jordan了。

cues.en: This one template for competitive greatness became so ubiquitous that we almost forgot there were ever any others.
cues.zh: 这个关于竞争伟大的单一模板变得如此普遍，以至于我们几乎忘了曾经还有别的模板。

cues.en: Part two.
cues.zh: 第二部分。

cues.en: So are you just gonna keep ranting about basketball
cues.zh: 所以你是要一直吐槽篮球吗

cues.en: or...
cues.zh: 还是……

cues.en: No. I'm going somewhere with this. Because now I'd like to talk about World of Warcraft,
cues.zh: 不。我这是有目的的。因为现在我想聊聊《魔兽世界》，

cues.en: the Michael Jordan of Mamorpeggers.
cues.zh: 大型多人在线角色扮演游戏里的迈克尔·乔丹。

cues.en: Like Jordan, Wow was very good at what it did. Like Jordan, it became a cultural phenomenon and captured the imaginations of a much wider audience than ever before.
cues.zh: 和乔丹一样，WoW 在本职上非常出色。和乔丹一样，它成为一种文化现象，俘获了远超前人的更广泛受众的想象力。

cues.en: Like Jordan, it made a shit ton of money, and like Michael Jordan, it ruined everything without even meaning to.
cues.zh: 和乔丹一样，它赚了海量的钱，也和迈克尔·乔丹一样，它在无意之中毁掉了一切。

cues.en: To illustrate what I mean, let's fast forward to the present day. It's been more than eight years since Wow ruined everything, and MMOs can be divided into two broad categories,
cues.zh: 为了说明我的意思，让我们快进到今天。距离《魔兽世界》毁掉一切已经过去八年多，MMO 现在可以分为两大类，

cues.en: the theme park and the sandbox.
cues.zh: 主题公园型和沙盒型。

cues.en: The theme park MMO is one with a comparatively high level of control and direction on the part of the developer.
cues.zh: 主题公园型 MMO 是开发者对游戏有较高控制度和引导性的那一类。

cues.en: The player inhabits a world created by someone else, completes tasks designed by someone else, and mostly has the experience that the developer intends.
cues.zh: 玩家身处别人创造的世界，完成别人设计的任务，体验基本由开发者预设。

cues.en: This isn't necessarily a bad thing. Theme parks can be fun, and their more directed nature allows their creators to design entertaining set pieces and a more cohesive gameplay experience.
cues.zh: 这不一定是坏事。主题公园可以很有趣，而且它们更有导向性的设计让创作者能够设计出有趣的场景和更连贯的游戏体验。

cues.en: The original example is EverQuest, but there are many, many others. There's been City of Heroes, Matrix Online, Warhammer Online, Age of Conan, Rift, The Old Republic, Terra, Guild Wars two. The list goes on and on. All in all, a very well represented genre.
cues.zh: 最初的例子是《无尽的任务》，但还有很多很多其他游戏。有《英雄城市》、《黑客帝国Online》、《战锤Online》、《科南时代》、《裂隙》、《旧共和国》、《特拉》、《激战2》。名单还长着呢。总而言之，这是一个代表作品非常丰富的类型。

cues.en: On the other end of the scale, you have the sandbox.
cues.zh: 另一头则是沙盒。

cues.en: Like the name implies, the sandbox style MMO allows for more freedom and creativity,
cues.zh: 顾名思义，沙盒风格的MMO给予更多自由和创造力，

cues.en: but also expects the players to provide their own direction.
cues.zh: 但也期望玩家自己提供方向。

cues.en: There's no shortage of sandbox MMOs these days either. You have Eve online. You have,
cues.zh: 如今沙盒MMO也不缺。有《Eve Online》。还有，

cues.en: let's see. So there's Eve and
cues.zh: 让我想想。所以有Eve和

cues.en: drawing a blank here. Jeez.
cues.zh: 这里卡壳了。天哪。

cues.en: I guess there's just Eve as far as major examples go, And Eve isn't even a great example. It's more like a high sec theme park surrounded by an optional null sec sandbox. Why is one type of MMO so much better represented than the other?
cues.zh: 就主要例子而言，我猜也就Eve了，而且Eve甚至不算好例子。它更像是一个被可选null sec沙盒包围的高sec主题公园。为什么一种类型的MMO比另一种代表性高这么多？

cues.en: I'll tell you why. Because World of Warcraft ruined everything.
cues.zh: 我来告诉你为什么。因为《魔兽世界》毁了一切。

cues.en: You see, Wow is the definitive example of a theme park MMO, and I'm using the word definitive deliberately.
cues.zh: 你看，WoW 是主题公园式 MMO 的典型代表，我用“典型”这个词是故意的。

cues.en: It was so iconic and successful that it defined expectations
cues.zh: 它太具标志性、太成功了，以至于它定义了人们对

cues.en: for the entire genre.
cues.zh: 整个品类的期待。

cues.en: It was a phenomenon. At one point, it had over 60 gajillion subscribers in China alone. Its revenue allowed Blizzard to buy the entire planet of Jupiter. It was the first PC game to be mentioned by Jesus himself.
cues.zh: 它是一个现象级作品。它一度仅在中国就有超过六百亿亿订阅用户。它的收入让暴雪买下了整个木星。它是第一款被耶稣本人提及的 PC 游戏。

cues.en: One of the reasons it had such a strong gravitational pull on the industry is because it was almost absurdly lucrative.
cues.zh: 它对整个行业产生如此强大的吸引力，原因之一是它几乎 absurdly 赚钱。

cues.en: It had access to a revenue stream that was catnip to investors and businessmen.
cues.zh: 它拥有一条让投资者和商人趋之若鹜的收入来源。

cues.en: Tell these people that they can charge $60 for their game and $15 a month to play it and their eyes do that cash register thing like you see in the cartoons.
cues.zh: 告诉这些人，他们的游戏可以卖 60 美元，每月还能收 15 美元来玩，他们的眼睛就会像卡通片里那样闪现出收银机的光芒。

cues.en: To compete with cats that fat, you had to raise huge amounts of capital and no one wanted to gamble that much money on anything but a sure thing. So caution was the order of the day, which meant that copying Wow was the order of the day.
cues.zh: 要与那么肥的猫竞争，你必须筹集巨额资金，而没人愿意在除了稳赚不赔的事情上赌那么多钱。所以谨慎成了当时的常态，这意味着照搬《魔兽世界》成了当时的常态。

cues.en: Of course, all these games were quick to claim that they weren't copying it. In fact, they were so determined to avoid copying it on a superficial level that they never noticed they were taking nearly all of its gameplay premises for granted.
cues.zh: 当然，这些游戏都急忙声称自己并没有抄袭它。事实上，它们如此坚决地避免在表面上抄袭，以至于从未注意到自己几乎把它所有的玩法前提都当成了理所当然。

cues.en: How many of these games have the same perspective, the same camera, the same hotbar and menus, the same Quest Hub centered gameplay, the same Gather 10 Wolf Ears quest, the same type of level based character advancement, the same type of optional crafting, the same type of regimented and isolated PvP?
cues.zh: 这些游戏中有多少拥有相同的视角、相同的镜头、相同的快捷栏和菜单、相同的以任务中心为核心的玩法、相同的“收集10只狼耳”任务、相同类型的基于等级的角色成长、相同类型的可选制作、相同类型的严格且孤立的PvP？

cues.en: Nearly all of them do. Deviations from the formula are limited and rare. It's not like they were imitating Wow on purpose. Instead, it was like a huge chunk of the development world just collectively forgot that an MMO can be any other way.
cues.zh: 几乎所有人都这么做。偏离这套公式的情况有限且罕见。他们并不是在刻意模仿《魔兽世界》。更像是开发界的一大部分人集体忘了，MMO还可以是别的样子。

cues.en: But there are other ways. Back in the olden days, before Wow ruined everything, the most popular and fondly remembered games had much more variety.
cues.zh: 但还有别的做法。回到远古时代，在《魔兽世界》毁掉一切之前，最受欢迎、最令人怀念的游戏种类要丰富得多。

cues.en: Just like basketball back in the day had Kareem, Magic and Bird, Mammorpigurs had RuneScape and Star Wars Galaxies and Ultima Online.
cues.zh: 就像当年的篮球有贾巴尔、魔术师约翰逊和伯德，MMO也有《RuneScape》、《星球大战：银河》和《网络创世纪》。

cues.en: All of these games had in them what we today would call sandbox elements.
cues.zh: 这些游戏都包含我们今天所说的沙盒元素。

cues.en: They didn't call them that back then because they didn't have to. MMOs were still in their formative stages and today's distinctions hadn't yet calcified.
cues.zh: 当时他们不这么叫，因为没必要。MMO还处在形成阶段，今天的分类尚未固化。

cues.en: Then Blizzard came along and proceeded to refine the formula by making a series of smart design choices, choices that were appropriate for the specific game Blizzard was making, not necessarily for the genre as a whole.
cues.zh: 然后暴雪出现了，通过一系列聪明的设计选择来完善这个模式，这些选择适合暴雪正在制作的特定游戏，而不一定适合整个类型。

cues.en: And, of course, in the process, they ruined everything. The myriad fascinating and exciting possibilities suggested by a group of people inhabiting the same virtual space were narrowed down to variations on a single template.
cues.zh: 当然，在这个过程中，他们毁掉了一切。一群人共处同一虚拟空间所暗示的无数迷人而激动人心的可能性，被窄化成单一模板的各种变体。

cues.en: Part three, why I'm so grumpy about this.
cues.zh: 第三部分，我为什么对此如此不满。

cues.en: This might seem like a bunch of aimless whining, which to be fair is kind of my thing. After all, if you don't like Wow, you don't have to play it. Right? And you don't have to play any of its various knockoffs either.
cues.zh: 这看起来可能像一堆漫无目的的抱怨，公平地说，这确实算是我的风格。毕竟，如果你不喜欢《魔兽世界》，你不玩就是了。对吧？你也不必去玩它的各种仿制品。

cues.en: The problem is that here in our irritatingly imperfect world, we have limited development resources. And in a sense, every Wow clone that gets made represents a more imaginative game not getting made.
cues.zh: 问题在于，在这个令人恼火的不完美世界里，我们的开发资源是有限的。从某种意义上说，每制作出一款《魔兽世界》的克隆作品，就意味着少了一款更有想象力的游戏被做出来。

cues.en: To describe what we're missing out on, I'm going to sneak into the graveyard of gaming criticism to exhume a discredited and unfashionable
cues.zh: 为了说明我们错过了什么，我要悄悄潜入游戏批评的墓地，挖掘出一个声名扫地、不再时兴的

cues.en: term, emergent gameplay.
cues.zh: 术语：涌现式玩法。

cues.en: I can already hear you groaning.
cues.zh: 我已经能听到你们的抱怨了。

cues.en: This term is unfortunately associated with Peter Molyneux, a developer who has a habit of promising the world and then failing to deliver.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，这个术语总和 Peter Molyneux 联系在一起，这位开发者习惯于许诺整个世界，然后却兑现不了。

cues.en: It's also generally associated with single player games. However, I would say that it's most useful when discussing sandbox style MMOs.
cues.zh: 它通常也和单机游戏联系在一起。不过我觉得，它最适合用来讨论沙盒式MMO。

cues.en: Let's go back to Eve. The outer reaches of the Eve world are a giant sandbox made of conquerable space collectively referred to as Nullsec.
cues.zh: 回到《Eve》。Eve世界的外围区域是一个巨大的沙盒，由可征服的太空构成，统称为Nullsec。

cues.en: Nullsec was its own world and as such developed its own culture complete with its own unspoken rules, habits, indicators of prestige and cultural norms.
cues.zh: Nullsec自成一体，因此发展出了自己的文化，包括不成文的规则、习惯、声望标志和文化规范。

cues.en: This world came to be dominated by a player alliance called Band of Brothers, which controlled what was at the time the most valuable space in the game.
cues.zh: 这个世界逐渐被一个叫Band of Brothers的玩家联盟所主宰，它控制了当时游戏中最宝贵的地盘。

cues.en: Then, an outside foreign culture, that of the Something Awful forums,
cues.zh: 后来，一种外来文化，即Something Awful论坛的文化，

cues.en: immigrated en masse into this world and began butting heads with Band of Brothers in what could be described as a tribal or sectarian conflict.
cues.zh: 大规模移民进入这个世界，并开始与Band of Brothers发生冲突，可以说是一场部落或教派间的争斗。

cues.en: It wasn't long before things got completely out of hand. What started as an elaborate proxy war became an elaborate direct war on a massive virtual scale, complete with drama, plot twists, internal conflict, its own propaganda, shifting alliances, espionage, intrigue, and sudden reversals of fortune.
cues.zh: 没过多久，事态就完全失控了。最初精心策划的代理战争，演变成了一场大规模虚拟层面的精心策划的直接战争，伴随着戏剧性事件、剧情反转、内部冲突、自己的宣传、联盟变换、间谍活动、阴谋诡计以及命运的突然逆转。

cues.en: The stakeholders in this conflict numbered in the tens of thousands and it went on for years.
cues.zh: 这场冲突涉及的参与者数以万计，持续了数年之久。

cues.en: Taken in its entirety, the war between Goonswarm and Band of Brothers is quite possibly the single most interesting thing to ever happen in a video game.
cues.zh: 整体来看，Goonswarm 与 Band of Brothers 之间的战争，很可能是电子游戏史上发生过的最有意思的一件事。

cues.en: EVE's developers did not design this war. They didn't steer players toward it or direct it in any way. I doubt many of them anticipated that their game would ever play host to anything this complex or on this massive a scale. It all happened on its own. It was all emergent.
cues.zh: EVE 的开发者并没有设计这场战争。他们没有引导玩家走向它，也没有以任何方式指挥它。我怀疑他们中很少有人预料到，自己的游戏竟能承载如此复杂、如此大规模的局面。这一切都是自发产生的。完全是涌现出来的。

cues.en: I'm asking you, please don't wince when you hear this word. This word is an appropriate description of what happened in Eve and of what continues to happen to this day. It's also something that could never have happened in a theme park, which means it could never have happened in most MMOs.
cues.zh: 我请求你们，听到这个词时别皱眉头。这个词恰当地描述了Eve中发生的事，以及至今仍在继续发生的事。这也是主题公园里绝不可能发生的事，意味着在大多数MMO中也绝不可能发生。

cues.en: This is what we've been missing out on in our rush to make 17 different versions of Wow.
cues.zh: 这就是我们在急于制作17个不同版本的Wow时错过的东西。

cues.en: At this point, you may be thinking, but I don't want to play Eve. I hear it super hard and everyone there will hate me and that I'll be staring at spreadsheets the whole time.
cues.zh: 此时，你可能会想，但我不想玩Eve。我听说它超级难，那里的每个人都会讨厌我，我会一直盯着电子表格。

cues.en: First, you should know that EVE's reputation for impenetrability
cues.zh: 首先要知道，EVE 高深莫测的名声

cues.en: and cruelty is exaggerated largely by its players themselves who are eager for everyone to know how space tough they are.
cues.zh: 和残酷的名声，很大程度上是被玩家自己夸大的，他们急于让所有人知道自己在太空里有多硬核。

cues.en: Second, these qualities are incidental to the game's sandbox nature, not fundamental to them. There's no requirement that sandbox style MMOs be opaque and unforgiving.
cues.zh: 其次，这些特性只是游戏沙盒本质的附带产物，而非根本要素。沙盒类 MMO 并不必然晦涩难懂、毫不宽容。

cues.en: There could be one that's just as accessible as any other type of game. There could and there should.
cues.zh: 完全可以有一款和其他类型游戏一样易上手的沙盒 MMO。可以，也应该有。

cues.en: There should have been four or five different EVEs by now, not just the same one we've been playing since 2003.
cues.zh: 到现在本该有四五个不同的EVE了，而不是我们从2003年一直玩到现在的同一个。

cues.en: Instead, it's like the genre has been on a treadmill for the past eight years, running endlessly and going nowhere.
cues.zh: 相反，这个类型在过去八年里就像在跑步机上，无尽地奔跑却哪儿也没去。

cues.en: Part four. How to unruin everything.
cues.zh: 第四部分。如何毁掉一切再挽救回来。

cues.en: All is not yet lost. Fortunately,
cues.zh: 一切尚未失去。幸运的是，

cues.en: there are brilliant minds like mine willing to give crucial advice that I assume everyone is eager to hear.
cues.zh: 有像我这样聪明的人愿意给出关键建议，我猜大家都迫不及待想听。

cues.en: Everyone is eager to hear it. Right?
cues.zh: 大家都迫不及待想听了。对吧？

cues.en: I'll take your silence as a yes. Here's what to do.
cues.zh: 我把你们的沉默当作是同意。接下来这么做。

cues.en: One, embrace the sandbox
cues.zh: 第一，拥抱沙盒

cues.en: because it has more advantages than you might realize.
cues.zh: 因为它带来的好处比你想象的要多。

cues.en: I'll explain. In an MMO, the players are part of the game. You want to keep them coming back. And the best way to keep them coming back is to keep adding new content.
cues.zh: 我来解释一下。在大型多人在线游戏里，玩家是游戏的一部分。你想让他们不断回来。而让他们不断回来的最好办法，就是不断添加新内容。

cues.en: This leads to a fundamental problem with the theme park, which is that not even the biggest team with the best managed pipeline in the business can ever create content as fast as players can play it.
cues.zh: 这就引出了主题公园模式的一个根本问题：即便是业内规模最大、流程管理最出色的团队，也永远无法像玩家消耗内容那样快地创造内容。

cues.en: The industry habit has been to solve this problem by turning the grind up to 11, by putting hours of busywork between the players and whatever goodies you're drip feeding them. But this is a clumsy solution.
cues.zh: 行业的习惯做法是把刷的强度开到 11，在玩家和你要一点点喂给他们的奖励之间塞进好几个小时的无聊苦工。但这是个笨拙的解法。

cues.en: The Sandbox Method sidesteps this problem by making the activity of players the content.
cues.zh: Sandbox 方法绕开了这个问题，它让玩家自身的活动成为内容。

cues.en: You don't have to build them a roller coaster. Just give them the tools and the raw materials and they'll build it themselves. You get a much better gameplay return per unit of development resources invested.
cues.zh: 你不用给他们造过山车。只要给他们工具和原材料，他们自己就会造出来。每投入一份开发资源，你能得到的玩法回报要好得多。

cues.en: You'd think developers would be chomping at the bit to exploit this dynamic, and after this video changes the industry forever, they probably will be.
cues.zh: 你会以为开发者会迫不及待地利用这种动态，而在这段视频永远改变行业之后，他们很可能就会这么做。

cues.en: Two, blur the line between multiplayer and MMO.
cues.zh: 第二，模糊多人游戏和大型多人在线游戏之间的界限。

cues.en: Massively multiplayer,
cues.zh: 大型多人在线，

cues.en: as a category of games, has acquired a lot of unnecessary baggage over the years. By contrast, multiplayer games are a laboratory of innovation.
cues.zh: 作为一种游戏类别，多年来积累了许多不必要的包袱。相比之下，多人游戏则是创新的实验室。

cues.en: Two of the most interesting games in recent memory are Minecraft and DayZ.
cues.zh: 近期最有趣的两款游戏是 Minecraft 和 DayZ。

cues.en: Neither of them is massively multiplayer,
cues.zh: 它们都不是大型多人在线的，

cues.en: but I don't see any reason why some of their basic gameplay concepts couldn't be scaled upwards.
cues.zh: 但我觉得它们的一些基本玩法概念没理由不能向上扩展。

cues.en: For that matter, I don't see any crucial reason to separate multiplayer that's massive from multiplayer that's just large or maybe medium sized. There's a wealth of possibilities between the two categories.
cues.zh: 既然如此，我也看不出有什么关键理由要把大型多人在线和只是大型或中等规模的多人在线分开。这两类之间存在大量可能性。

cues.en: Three,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: keep it manageable.
cues.zh: 保持可控。

cues.en: If you were going to assign a tragic flaw to the MMO industry, it would definitely be hubris.
cues.zh: 如果要给 MMO 行业定一个悲剧性缺陷，那肯定是傲慢。

cues.en: These games are expected to be big. They're expected to have big teams, big budgets and big ambitions.
cues.zh: 这些游戏预计规模宏大，它们预期拥有大团队、大预算和宏大野心。

cues.en: This means a big investment to recoup, which means they're going to tend towards being cautious and therefore tend towards being derivative.
cues.zh: 这意味着巨额投资需要回收，因此它们倾向于谨慎行事，进而倾向于模仿跟风。

cues.en: Fortunately,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: after a half dozen expensive flops, the allure of making the Wow killer has faded and the rise of free to play games has created a more itinerant customer base. There's now room for five one hundred pound gorillas and not just one five hundred pound one.
cues.zh: 在几款昂贵失败作品之后，制作“魔兽杀手”的诱惑已消退，免费游戏的兴起造就了更流动的用户群。现在可容纳五个百磅大猩猩，而非仅一个五百磅的。

cues.en: So, game industry, follow these steps and you will unlock the potential of multiplayer games, Potential that, in my opinion, is still frustratingly
cues.zh: 所以，游戏行业，遵循这些步骤，你就能释放多人游戏的潜力，而在我看来，这种潜力仍然令人沮丧地

cues.en: untapped.
cues.zh: 未被开发。

cues.en: Coming up. If any of you've been waiting for the video that ties all of it together, the one that unifies everything I've been saying so far into a single thesis, into what you could consider my manifesto,
cues.zh: 接下来。如果你们中有人一直在等那个把所有内容串联起来的视频，那个把我迄今为止所说的一切统一成一个单一论点、统一成你可以称之为我的宣言的视频，

cues.en: the video that will radically change the way you look at gaming from the ground up?
cues.zh: 那个将从根本上彻底改变你看待游戏方式的视频？

cues.en: If so, then you are out of luck because I don't have any plans to do anything like that. I mean, can you imagine how hard that would be? It would be super hard.
cues.zh: 如果是这样，那你可就不走运了，因为我没有任何做那种事的计划。我是说，你能想象那有多难吗？那会超级难。

cues.en: But, have any of you been waiting for me to make a video about an obscure eighteenth century novelist and how his work relates to gaming today?
cues.zh: 但是，你们中有没有人一直在等我做一个关于一位鲜为人知的十八世纪小说家以及他的作品如何与当今游戏相关联的视频？

cues.en: If so, then this time you are in luck because that's what I'm gonna do. It'll be out sometime before Half Life three.
cues.zh: 如果是这样，那么这次你可就走运了，因为那就是我要做的事。它会在《半条命3》发布之前的某个时候推出。
